sample_unit: open-source LLMs evaluated on synthetic safety-classification tasks

links.outcome: False-negative rates of LLMs detecting suicidal ideation, therapy requests, and therapy-like interactions in synthetic chatbot conversations
links.effect: Frequent errors in suicidal-ideation and therapy-like interactions; estimated P1 ranged 2.0×10-8 to 2.6×10-4 and P2 from 7.1×10-5 to 9.6×10-3, spanning up to four orders of magnitude across 14 models.
links.quote: LLM success at generating synthetic safety datasets varied substantially by task, with strong performance for neutral and non-therapeutic content but frequent errors in suicidal-ideation and therapy-like interactions.

unlisted_practices: Simulation-based estimation of hazard-to-harm probabilities (P1, P2) integrated into SaMD risk analysis for LLM devices
Using LLM-generated synthetic datasets verified by psychiatrists to test safety classification

screen.reason: Empirical study developing and testing a simulation framework to quantify safety hazards and harm risks (e.g., suicidal ideation detection) for LLM-based medical devices using synthetic patient interactions.

primary.practice: simulation-based pre-deployment risk estimation and safety testing
